Three Rivers Admin Handbook

For everyone who edits the website

How the Three Rivers website is put together, and where to make each change.

This handbook covers how this site's admin is set up: which record owns each piece of content, how pages and services work, and how to publish safely. Edit content on the live site only.

Chapter 01 of 14 · Start here

The admin at a glance

Signing in, the dashboard, the sidebar, and why content is edited only on the live site.

Sign in on the live site

Edit content at https://www.threeriversmentalhealth.com/admin and nowhere else. The live admin holds the site's real content. Local copies of the site are for development and are never a source of content. Code and design changes go through Andy.

Your account in Users has a Name. The dashboard greets you with it and uses it to label your saves under Recent changes. Without one, your email shows there instead. Activity and Last edited by always record your email. If you can't sign in, ask Andy.

The dashboard

The dashboard is the admin's home page. The practice logo at the top of the sidebar always brings you back to it.

  • Open the site opens the public website in a new tab. Go straight to links to the pages that hold the Home, Team and Services roles in Site Settings, then to Site Settings and Upload media.
  • Clinicians shows the team by role, with photos. Pick someone to change their photo, bio or availability. A small tag marks anyone who is private, coming soon or not plainly accepting new patients.
  • Pages lists every page grouped by address: main pages first, then one column for each address that has pages under it. A dot marks a page saved in the last seven days, and Private marks pages hidden from visitors.
  • Recent changes groups saves by person, newest first. All activity opens the full log.
  • Practice details lists the shared records: Services, Fees, Insurance Plans, FAQs, Site Settings, Header, Footer and Media. Each is edited in one place, and every page that shows it updates. The collections have Add (Upload for Media). The Services Add starts a new service page (see Services).
  • Programs links to each program's settings and to the Program tracks and Program groups lists.
  • Behind the scenes holds old addresses (Redirects), who can sign in (Users), the full change log (Activity) and content migrations. You'll rarely need it.

The sidebar

The sidebar starts with two links of its own. Services lists the service pages, and Program settings opens a page of links to each program's records (see Virtual IOP and programs). Below them, records sit in four groups:

  • Website holds Pages, Media, Header and Footer.
  • Practice holds Clinicians, Insurance Plans, Fees, FAQs and Site Settings.
  • Programs holds Program tracks and Program groups.
  • Behind the scenes holds Redirects, Users, Activity and Content migrations.

Where content lives explains what each one owns.

Reading a form

Help text sits under each field. Long help shows its first sentence with Read more. Lists and page sections open collapsed, so you see their row names first. Show All expands every row.

The Admin strip on public pages

While you're signed in, public pages show a dark Admin strip above the site header. It names the page or profile you're looking at and offers Edit this page or Edit this profile, plus Dashboard. Hide tucks it away until you close the tab, and the Admin button in the bottom corner brings it back. Visitors never see the strip.

Saving while the site updates

While new code is being deployed, a save can briefly answer "The website is being updated. Your changes are still on screen; save again in a minute." That's expected. Wait a minute and press Save again. Your edits stay in the form.

Chapter 02 of 14 · Start here

Where content lives

Which record owns each piece of content, so one edit updates every page that shows it.

One record for each fact

Each piece of shared content is stored in one record, and every page that shows it reads it from there, so one edit updates them all. Before you change wording on a page, find the record that holds it. A phone number, fee or credential retyped into a page section stops following the real one.

What each record owns

  • Pages hold their own sections and wording, Title, address, Parent page, Featured Image, Card title and Card summary. See Pages and sections.
  • Services are pages with This page is a service ticked. Each also holds the service's Tag, Summary, Order and Care pathways, plus a Program facts group that only structured programs such as the Virtual IOP fill in. See Services.
  • Clinicians hold each person's name, credentials, title, role, photo, bio, profile sections, Services provided, availability and order. See Clinicians.
  • Media holds uploaded photos, logos and videos with their Description / alt text and captions. A change here shows everywhere the item is used. See Photos and video.
  • FAQs are named groups of questions. Fees hold each fee's amount and notes. Insurance Plans hold each plan and what it covers. See FAQs, fees and insurance.
  • Program tracks hold each track's label and order, and Program groups hold each group's description and weekly sessions. See Virtual IOP and programs.
  • Site Settings holds the practice name and logos, phone, email, locations, the safety notice, shared button wording, patient destinations, clinician role titles, page roles and the private lists.
  • Header and Footer hold the site's navigation and the links at the bottom of every page. See Site Settings, header and footer.

What a page chooses

Many sections pick records instead of holding text. The section decides which records appear, and the record supplies the words.

  • Service grid shows every service in its Full layout, or the services chosen in Services shown in the other layouts. Either way it uses each service's card text and photo.
  • Care team shows the clinicians whose Services provided include the chosen service.
  • Care pathways shows the Care pathways rows saved on the chosen service.
  • FAQ list shows the FAQ groups you choose, in order.
  • Fee list and the self-pay card in Insurance panel read from Fees.
  • Locations reads the locations in Site Settings, and Contact panel reads its phone, email and patient destinations.
  • Safety notice shows the shared crisis line from Site Settings → Safety notice.
  • Clinician spotlight takes the name, title, credentials and photo from the chosen clinician.
  • Page cards show each chosen page's Card title, Card summary and Featured Image.

Links follow the record

When a link field offers A page or clinician profile or A patient destination, choose the record. The link then follows the page if it moves, and a patient destination's address changes in one place. Writing on this site covers link fields and shared button text.

Records in use stay put

The admin refuses to delete a record that other content still uses, such as a page, clinician, FAQ group or Media item. Its message says the record "is still used" and lists each place that uses it. Change those places, then try again. The same rule keeps a patient destination while links still use it, and keeps This page is a service ticked while anything still chooses that service.

Chapter 03 of 14 · Pages

Pages and sections

Page designs, adding and ordering sections, and the shared treatment design.

A page's own fields

Title names the page in the admin, in breadcrumbs and on its cards, unless Card title replaces it on cards. Slug sets the address, which changes after the first save only through Change slug… (see Addresses and moving pages). Parent page, in the sidebar, places the page in a section of the site. Breadcrumbs follow it, but it doesn't change the address. This page is a service, also in the sidebar, is covered in Services.

Page design

Page design sets how the whole page is laid out.

  • Individual page design lets each section keep its own design choices.
  • Treatment gives the page the shared treatment design described below. The page keeps its own copy, photos and section order.
  • Chapters turns the first Hero into a shorter header, then numbers each Section text, FAQ list, Program groups, Comparison table, Insurance panel and Fee list section that has a heading. Wide screens list them in a page index. Those sections take the chapter look, and their own layout and color choices are hidden and kept for switching back. Override Sidebar CTA Card gives this page a contact card that differs from the one set in the Header.
  • Hub opens with the same shorter header, for pages that lead to others, such as a list of conditions. Every section after it keeps its own design.

Add and arrange sections

The Layout field holds the page's sections, top to bottom. Add Layout opens the section picker. Each row's header shows its number, its type and a name taken from the section's heading. Type in the name box only to give the row a different name in the admin.

The row menu has Move Up, Move Down, Duplicate, Add Below and Remove, and you can drag rows. A page needs at least one section. A new service page is the exception: it gets the standard service sections when first saved.

The picker offers 33 section types. Those that pick records, such as Care team or Fee list, take their words from those records (see Where content lives).

Many sections have a Section name, which lets a link open that part of the page as "/page#name". Names are unique on a page. Links follow a rename, and the admin won't remove a name while links elsewhere still open it.

The shared treatment design

On a treatment page, Hero, Section text, Premise, Journey timeline, Care team, FAQ list and Care pathways each show a Design scope control. With Shared treatment design chosen, the section shows shared style choices such as Hero background or Section text background. Site Settings stores them, so a change applies to every treatment page that uses the shared design. Live Preview shows the change before you save it.

Save shared design saves these choices for every page, and Discard design changes drops them. The page's Save button doesn't save them. Open Used on to see which saved pages follow the design.

Choose Customize for this page to give one section its own look. It starts from the current shared look and saves with the page. Choose Shared treatment design again to reconnect it.

Section text on a treatment page also has an Appointment prompt: Shared treatment prompt, Customize for this section or No appointment prompt. The shared prompt has its own Save shared prompt button.

Chapter 04 of 14 · Pages

Editing from the preview

Clicking text in the live preview, and which record opens.

Open the preview

After a page's first save, press Live Preview, the button with an eye icon near Save. The page appears beside the form and follows your unsaved edits as you type, and the button changes to Exit Live Preview. Save updates the site, and View page opens the saved page in a new tab.

Drag the divider between the form and the preview to resize them. Arrow keys also move it, and a double-click resets it. The size menu in the preview toolbar starts at Responsive and switches to Mobile, Tablet or Desktop.

Select to edit

Press Select to edit in the preview toolbar, then move over the page. Each part you can open is outlined. When a frame opens a whole section, its tag reads Edit section. For the site header or footer as a whole, it reads Edit header or Edit footer.

Click the part, or tab to it and press Enter. Press Done selecting or Escape to stop. While selecting, links don't take you anywhere. A link with no editing field behind it says to turn off Select to edit to follow it.

Some parts have more than one owner, such as a sentence that includes the practice phone number. Those open a Choose what to edit list. For that sentence it offers Edit this sentence and Site Settings → Phone. Each choice carries a hint. "This opens the field that owns this content" means a field on this page. "Editing this source updates every use" means a shared record.

Where your click lands

A field on the page you're editing opens in the form beside the preview. The form opens the tab, group or section row that holds it, scrolls to it and outlines it for a moment.

Anything else opens in a side panel over the form. That includes Site Settings, the Header and Footer, a clinician, an FAQ group, a fee, an insurance plan, a program track or group, and other pages, such as one shown in a card. The panel's title names the record and field, for example:

  • The phone number opens Site Settings → Phone, and the email opens Site Settings → Email.
  • The logo opens Site Settings → Header logo or Footer logo.
  • Shared button wording opens Site Settings → Button text.

When a part can't be opened on its own, its whole section opens instead, and the toolbar tells you.

Saving in the side panel

The side panel holds that record's own form, with its own Save. That Save updates the live site and every page that shows the record, and the preview then refreshes around your page. Your unsaved page edits stay as they are, so save the page separately if you changed it.

If you close a panel with unsaved changes, the admin asks "Discard source changes?" Keep editing returns you to the panel. Discard source changes closes it and keeps your unsaved page edits. Only one panel opens at a time, so close it before opening another record.

Notes only editors see

The preview shows problems that visitors never see. A section that leaves something out lists it under "This section shows less than it should until this is fixed:". Text with problems shows "Fix these before publishing:". Fix what it lists, then check that the note has gone.

Chapter 05 of 14 · Pages

Services

Service pages: creating one, its card, care pathways and program facts.

A service is its page

A page with This page is a service ticked in its sidebar is the service. There is no separate service record. Its own fields supply what other pages show about it:

  • Title is the service's name in lists, pickers and breadcrumbs.
  • Card title and Card summary are its service card text, and care pathway links use the Card title. Left empty, they use the Title and the Summary.
  • Featured Image is its card photo, also used for social sharing.
  • The Private checkbox hides the page and the service together. See Private, publish and history.

Once ticked, the page appears wherever the site lists services, including clinicians' Services provided and the team filter. Pickers in Care team, Care pathways, Service grid and Program facts sections offer only service pages.

Finding a service

Services in the sidebar opens the Pages list filtered to service pages. The dashboard's Services row, under Practice details, opens the same list and has an Add link.

The Service listing group

The Service listing group sets how the service appears in lists, cards and care pathways.

  • Tag is optional: a short fact the name doesn't say, such as "In-office, supervised". It appears with the name on service cards.
  • Summary is the fuller description in the Full and Featured service lists. Cards use the Card summary when it's filled.
  • Order sets the position in service lists and the team filter. Lower numbers come first.
  • Care pathways link to related services. Each row picks a Service and needs a Reason: one sentence on when or why that service is the next step. Each row is labelled by the service it leads to.

Every service page also has a Program facts group, which only structured programs such as the Virtual IOP use. See Virtual IOP and programs.

Adding a service

The quickest start is Add on the dashboard's Services row. It opens a new page already marked as a service, with /services/ greyed before the slug and Treatment chosen under Page design. You can also press Create New in the Services list or the Pages list, then tick This page is a service before the first save.

Enter the title and slug, then save without adding sections. The page starts with:

  1. a Hero with the title;
  2. Care team, headed "Who you'd see";
  3. Intake steps, headed "What to expect";
  4. Care pathways, headed "If this isn't enough";
  5. Begin / CTA.

What to expect and Begin are copied from existing service pages, so their wording is the practice's own. Care team and Care pathways already point at the new service, but the site leaves them out until a clinician lists it under Services provided (see Clinicians) and you add pathway rows. Like every new page, it starts private, so nothing is public until you untick Private and save.

Changing or removing a service

You can't untick This page is a service while anything still chooses the page as a service. The save stops with "Still chosen as a service:" and lists the places. Choose another service in each, then untick it.

Chapter 06 of 14 · Pages

Addresses and moving pages

Slugs, the fixed part of an address, and Change slug with its redirects.

The slug is the address

A page's Slug is its address after the site name, such as services/tms. Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, with / only between segments, up to 100 characters. The site reserves addresses starting with /admin, /api or /_next, and addresses under the Team page belong to clinician profiles.

The part of the address a record's type fixes shows greyed in front of the box, and you type the rest. Most pages show /, a new service page shows /services/, and a clinician profile shows the Team page's address, such as /team/. The Virtual IOP keeps its own address, /virtual-iop.

The read-only Path in the sidebar shows where the page is published now. The site serves the page chosen as Home in Site Settings at "/". Renaming the Title never changes the address.

After the first save

Before the first save, the slug is an ordinary field. After it, the field shows the current address and a Change slug… button, which is the only way to change a saved address. Clinician profiles work the same way.

Changing a slug

  1. Save or discard any other changes first. The slug change saves on its own, and it won't run while the form has unsaved edits.
  2. Select Change slug… and type the New slug.
  3. Read What will happen. It lists: - the redirect from the old address to the new one, "so old links and bookmarks keep working"; - pages whose addresses sit under this one, where each would go, and a box (ticked at first) to move them too; - how many menu items and links chosen with the page picker follow automatically; - places that typed the old address by hand, each with a link so you can fix it. The redirect keeps them working meanwhile.
  4. Select Change slug. The page reloads with a "Slug changed" note and an Undo button that changes it back.

The Home page stays at "/", and the site sends links to its old slug address there. Changing the Team page's slug moves every clinician profile under the new address, and their old addresses redirect.

Parent page and the address

Parent page in the sidebar places a page in a section and sets its breadcrumbs. It never changes the address. The pages under it in the Change slug panel are pages whose slug starts with this one, whatever their Parent page.

Privacy follows Parent page, so moving a page out of a private section can make it public (see Private, publish and history).

Redirects

Redirects, under Behind the scenes, lists old addresses and where they send visitors. A slug change adds one with the reason Renamed in the CMS, and moves any redirects that pointed at the old address to the new one. Redirects you add yourself use Added by an editor, and the old site's addresses use Legacy site URL.

To add one, enter From (the old path, such as "/tms") and To (a current page path, or a full https:// address for an outside site). A path a live page uses can't redirect, and To must be a live address.

A new page that takes an address removes any redirect from it. Deleting a page deletes the redirects that point to it.

Chapter 07 of 14 · People and practice

Clinicians

Profiles, services provided, availability, photos and order.

One record per clinician

Each clinician is one record under Clinicians (Practice group). That record feeds the Team page, the clinician's profile, the care team on each service page and any Clinician spotlight section that chooses them.

The list is sorted by Order, and its Accepting new patients column shows availability in words.

Name, title and role

  • Name and Credentials show together on cards and the profile. Credentials are post-nominal letters, e.g. "MD" or "PMHNP-BC".
  • Title is optional. Without one, the profile shows the role's title from Site Settings → Clinicians → Clinician roles.
  • Role is Prescriber (MD / NP), Therapist (LICSW / LCSW) or Staff. The Team page groups clinicians by role, under the headings set in Clinician roles.
  • Slug is the profile address. The Team page part is fixed and shows greyed. After the first save, change it with Change slug… (see Addresses and moving pages).

Services provided

Services provided lists the service pages this clinician directly provides. A service page's care team, the profile's "Services provided" list and the team filter on the Team page all read it, so to add someone to a service's care team, edit the clinician.

A care team lists clinicians by role, then by Order.

Availability

  • Coming Soon shows a "Coming soon" badge in place of any availability.
  • Accepting new patients switches the standard line between "Accepting new patients" and "Not currently accepting new patients".
  • Availability note replaces the standard line, e.g. "Accepting new TMS patients". It is hidden while Coming Soon is on.

Team cards show the line for every role except Staff. The profile leaves it out for a clinician who isn't accepting and has no note. Hours is free text shown below it on cards and the profile.

Photo and profile text

Photo is the portrait. On the Team page, in care teams and on the profile, the site crops it to one tall shape and keeps the top of the photo, so a focal point set in Media doesn't move it there. A Clinician spotlight follows the focal point and reads the photo's Media description (see Photos and video). Without a photo the frame stays empty. Never fill it with another person's photo.

Bio starts a new paragraph at each blank line. With no bio, the profile shows one line giving the name, title and practice. Profile sections adds Section text, Entry list or Feature band content below the bio. Education lines appear under "Background", and Insurance Accepted lists plans under "Insurance accepted".

For search engines never shows on the profile. Keep its Certifications and Confirmed profiles elsewhere in step with what the profile says.

Order, privacy and shared links

Order sets the position on team grids, low to high.

New items start private on this site, so a new clinician starts with Private ticked (see Private, publish and history). A private clinician is left off the Team page, service pages and spotlights, and the profile isn't published. Untick Private and save when the profile is ready. View profile opens the profile, or its signed-in preview while it's private.

The back link, consultation button and team link on every profile come from Site Settings → Clinicians → Clinician profile links.

Chapter 08 of 14 · People and practice

FAQs, fees and insurance

Question groups that pages choose, fee amounts and insurance plans.

FAQ groups

A record under FAQs (Practice group) is a named group of questions. Pages show groups through an FAQ list section, which chooses one or more groups in order. When a section chooses more than one, each group's Title shows as a subheading.

Each question row has a Question and an Answer. The answer is the direct reply, shown first. Two more fields are optional:

  • Sources for the answer. Each source has a title, an optional publisher and an optional https:// address. Sources are numbered after the text and listed at the end of the section.
  • More content, which adds Paragraph, List and Links items after the answer in the order you set.

Saving a group updates every page that shows it. The page also passes its questions and answers to search engines, built from the same text. To reuse questions on another page, choose the same group in that page's FAQ list. Copying the text into a new group leaves two versions to keep in step.

You can't delete a group that a page still chooses (see Where content lives).

Fees

Each record under Fees is one amount, with four fields:

  • Service is the fee's name as visitors read it. It's plain text and doesn't link to a service page.
  • Price is also text, so write it exactly as it should appear.
  • Notes is optional text about that fee.
  • Order sets the default position.

Fees show up in three places:

  • A Fee list section shows the fees it chooses, in the order chosen. If it chooses none, it shows every fee by Order. Each fee's notes appear under its name.
  • An Insurance panel can add a self-pay card through its Pricing fields. The card shows each chosen fee's service and price, without the notes.
  • Text fields can insert a fee's price or notes as a global value (see Writing on this site).

Change an amount on the fee record. Retyping it into page text leaves a copy that won't follow the next change.

Insurance plans

Insurance Plans holds the plans the practice accepts. Every Insurance panel lists all of them, sorted by Order. A page can't show only some of them.

  • Name is the plan as visitors read it.
  • Notes shows beside the plan in place of the panel's badge. The badge is the panel's Payer Badge, "In-network" unless the panel changes it.
  • Scope is Full (all services) or Medication management only. A medication-only plan can't be saved without a note, so the limit is always visible, e.g. "Medication management only". Visitors see the note. Scope itself isn't shown.

Clinicians choose plans in Insurance Accepted on their own record, and the profile lists them (see Clinicians).

Live as soon as you save

FAQ groups, fees and insurance plans have no Private checkbox, so a saved change is public at once (see Private, publish and history). Change a fee or plan only once the practice has confirmed the new details, and ask Andy if you're not sure.

Chapter 09 of 14 · People and practice

Virtual IOP and programs

Program settings, program facts, tracks, groups and the schedule.

Where program content lives

A structured program such as the Virtual IOP is a service page plus three kinds of record:

  • Program facts, a group of fields on the service page itself.
  • Program tracks (Programs group in the sidebar), which organize a program's groups, e.g. separate patient and caregiver tracks.
  • Program groups, each with its own descriptions and weekly sessions.

Pages show them through the Program facts, Program groups and Program schedule sections. Each reads from the service it chooses.

Program settings

Program settings sits in the sidebar below Services. You edit nothing on it. Choose a Program and select Open program to list its tracks and groups, each linking to its record, with a link to the service page's Program facts. A service appears in the list once its Program facts hold a value or a track belongs to it.

Program facts

Program facts appears on every service page, below Service listing, but only structured programs use it. Leave it empty for ordinary services.

  • Format is how the program is delivered, e.g. "Live video groups".
  • Minimum age is a whole number. Leave it empty when no age is stated, since 0 counts as a value.
  • Who it's for takes one short approved label per row. Leave the age out; it has its own field. Each row's Sentence wording sets how it reads after "for" in a composed sentence. Editing the label doesn't change it, so update both when the audience changes.
  • Where lists the states served, in order. A row can choose that state's page. The state name then links to it, and a This state section on that page shows only that state.
  • Topic cycle is how long topics run before repeating, and Program length is how long someone stays.
  • The group also holds Included care, Schedule page, Time zone and Callbacks → Callback time.

Tracks and groups

A track has a Program, a Label and an Order. Its program can change only while it has no groups.

A group has a Track, a Name, a Summary (for Summary sections), a Description (for Details sections), Sessions, Related information and an Order. Two programs can have tracks with the same label, so check the Program column when choosing one. A group that a page selects can't move to another program's track or be deleted.

Each session needs a Day. Start and End use 24-hour HH:MM, e.g. 13:15, in the program's time zone, and the site never converts them. Leave unconfirmed times empty. The day still shows, marked "time to be confirmed". A time can't be saved until the service has a Time zone, and the time zone can't be cleared while any session has a time.

Tracks and groups have no Private checkbox. They go live when saved, unless their service page is private. While it is, check program changes in the page's preview (see Private, publish and history).

Sections on pages

  • In a Program facts section, Shows picks Summary, Eligibility, This state, Length or Included care. Facts with no value are left out. Notes add rows where the program has no fact yet. Once a matching fact exists, replace the note with it.
  • In Program groups and Program schedule sections, All follows the program, so new, renamed and reordered groups or tracks appear on their own. Selected shows only the ones you choose, in your order. Switching back to All clears the selection when you save.

Chapter 10 of 14 · Writing and media

Writing on this site

Text fields, practice facts in text, button wording, phone numbers and links.

Text in sections

Don't type facts the practice keeps in one place, such as the phone number, a fee or a program's length, into section text. Insert them as global values so they follow their source.

More content, where a field has it, holds Paragraph, List and Links items in your order. In a paragraph, select words and choose Add link to link them to a page or profile.

Global values

Most text fields in page sections, card text and SEO fields have an Insert global value button, and so do FAQ questions and answers. It offers values kept in one place:

  • Site Settings: Practice name, Phone, Email, Front desk email, Fax and Safety notice.
  • Each service's Program facts, such as Who it's for, Where (states), Format, Minimum age, Topic cycle and Program length.
  • Program tracks and groups: the days a track's groups meet, and a group's weekly schedule and session start times.
  • Each fee's Price and Fee notes.

The value appears in the text as a chip. Select a chip to edit its source without leaving the page, and saving the source updates every use. Refresh global values reloads them after a source changes elsewhere. If a value can't be read, for example because its source is empty, the whole text is left out until it's fixed, and the field shows why.

Composed text

A Hero can build its text from segments. Set Text under the headline to Composed, then add Words and Fact segments. Type Words exactly as they'll read, spaces included. A Fact names its source (Site Settings, a service's program or a program track), the fact, and how it's Written as. A line above shows the sentence as it reads now, or what stops it. A Care scale section works the same way through Text and level descriptions.

Button wording

Site Settings → Button text holds shared wording. Each row has a Name in the editor and the Text visitors see. A link's Button text picks a row, and editing that row updates every link using it. Tick Override button text to give one link its own words, or leave Button text empty and write the link's Label. You can't remove a button text that links still use.

Phone numbers

The practice number lives in Site Settings → Contact → Phone: a US number with area code, with any extension written as "ext. 12".

  • For a call link, set Link to to Call the practice and leave its text empty. Visitors see "Call" and the current number.
  • Sections with a Show Phone or Show phone number checkbox show the Site Settings number.
  • In running text, insert Phone as a global value. A typed number won't change when the practice number does.

Links

Link to has four choices:

  • A page or clinician profile links to the record you choose in Page or profile. Section can open a named section of that page. The link follows the page if its address changes (see Addresses and moving pages).
  • A patient destination links to an off-site patient tool listed in Site Settings → Patient destinations (see Site Settings, header and footer).
  • Another address takes a full https:// address, tel:, mailto:, or "#section" for a section of the same page. It refuses addresses on this site, so choose the page instead. Links to other sites open in a new tab.
  • Call the practice works as described under Phone numbers.

Chapter 11 of 14 · Writing and media

Photos and video

Uploading, alt text, focal points, featured images and checking crops.

The Media library

Media, in the Website group of the sidebar, holds every image and video the site uses. One Media item can appear in many places, and a change to it shows in all of them. Search the library before uploading, and reuse the item when it's the same picture.

Uploaded files stay public even when the page that uses them is private, and anyone with a file's address can open it. Never upload anything that has to stay confidential.

Uploading

Media accepts images and MP4 or WebM videos. Upload from Media, or from a photo field with Create New. Choose from existing reuses an item that's already there.

The site never shows a photo's original file. It shows WebP copies at most 1920 pixels wide and doesn't enlarge a smaller original, so a narrow photo can look soft in a wide spot. Videos keep their original quality, since the site doesn't compress them.

You can replace an item's file with one of the same kind, an image with an image or a video with a video. Every place that uses the item then shows the new file. To change the kind of file, upload a new Media item.

Description / alt text

Description / alt text is required. Describe what the picture shows. For images it's also the text screen readers read. The image, its description and any caption have to describe the same subject.

Some places use other text. A clinician portrait is announced by the clinician's name. A photo used as decoration, such as a Feature band photo with Photo Style set to Mood, isn't read aloud.

For a video with speech, add Captions (WebVTT). The text starts with the line "WEBVTT", then each caption sits under its timing line. Visitors turn captions on with the player's captions button.

Focal points and crops

Many frames crop a photo to fit their shape. Open Edit Image on the Media item and set the Focal Point to choose what those crops keep. A Feature band's Image Focus can set a different position for that one section.

Clinician portraits on the Team page, in care teams and on the profile ignore it and keep the top of the photo (see Clinicians).

Leave Crop alone unless you mean to change the file itself, everywhere it's used.

Featured images

A page's Featured Image is its main photo. A service page's cards use it, and it's the image for social sharing unless the page sets a Social image override. With neither, sharing uses Site Settings → Brand → Default OG image. On treatment pages the shared treatment design decides where the featured image sits (see Pages and sections).

If a chosen photo can't be shown because it was deleted, has no file or is a video in a photo spot, the section leaves it out and the preview says why. A Media item still in use can't be deleted (see Where content lives).

Chapter 12 of 14 · Publishing

Private, publish and history

The Private checkbox, going live, checking your work, and restoring a version.

The Private checkbox

Pages (service pages included) and clinicians have a Private checkbox beside Save. Ticked and saved, the record stays off the public site. Unticked and saved, it goes live. There are no drafts: Save updates the site straight away, so Private is how you keep a saved page from visitors.

Nothing else has one: FAQ groups, fees, insurance plans, program tracks and program groups go live when saved, though a private service page still hides its tracks and groups.

Site Settings → Publication → New items start private is on for this site. Every page, service page or clinician you add or duplicate starts with Private ticked, and stays hidden until someone unticks it and saves.

A page inside a private section shows Private via its section, ticked and locked. Change that on the section's own page, or in Site Settings → Publication.

What Private hides

Visitors who open a private page get the site's Page not found page (a 404). Public pages, menus, cards and the sitemap leave it out. A private service page also hides its cards, care pathway links, team filter entry, program facts, tracks and groups. Every page below a private page through Parent page is private too, whatever its address, so moving a page out of a private section can make it public.

Private doesn't hide uploaded files (see Photos and video).

The checkbox adds the record to, or removes it from, Private pages and sections or Private clinicians in Site Settings → Publication, so the save also saves Site Settings. If Site Settings has a field to fix, the save stops with "Not saved. The Private checkbox also saves Site Settings". Fix the field it names there, then save again.

Checking a private page

While a page is private, View page opens it in a signed-in preview, and Live Preview shows unsaved edits beside the form.

Going live

  1. Check the page in Live Preview at the Mobile, Tablet and Desktop sizes.
  2. Untick Private and save.
  3. Open the public address in a signed-out window.
  4. Check the places it should appear, such as service grids or the Team page. Adding it to the header or footer menus is a separate step (see Site Settings, header and footer).

Versions

Pages, clinicians, fees, insurance plans, FAQs, program tracks and groups, redirects, Site Settings, Header and Footer have a Versions tab. It keeps each item's latest 100 versions. Open one to compare it with the current content, then use Restore this version and confirm.

A restore is another save. It goes live straight away, the usual checks apply, and Activity records it as a restore. Media has no Versions tab, and Versions can't bring back a deleted item. Ask Andy if you need either.

Last edited by, in the sidebar, shows who saved the record last. Content saved before tracking began shows no editor until its next save.

Activity

Activity, under Behind the scenes, lists every saved change with its time, Changed by, action (create, update, restore, delete or transfer), Content type and item. Filter by editor, item or date, and open an entry to see each changed field before and after. Entries can't be edited or deleted, and unsaved Live Preview edits aren't recorded.

Chapter 13 of 14 · Publishing

Site Settings, header and footer

Practice details, locations, safety notice, button wording, navigation and footer.

Three site-wide records

Site Settings sits under Practice in the sidebar, and Header and Footer under Website. Each is one record for the whole site, so a save changes every page. Previews show their saved versions, so save before checking.

Site Settings

  • Publication holds New items start private, which is on, and the private lists. See Private, publish and history.
  • Analytics holds the Google Analytics measurement ID. Leave it empty to turn analytics off.
  • Brand holds the Practice name, Header logo, Footer logo, favicon, Default OG image, Color theme and Body font. The practice name also shows wherever a logo is missing.
  • Safety notice is the shared crisis line. Pages choose where it appears with a Safety notice section, and those sections hide while it's empty.
  • Contact holds Phone, Email, Front desk email, Fax and Locations. The Locations section and the footer read this list. Tick Practice address for search engines on one in-person location.
  • Button text holds shared button wording. See Writing on this site.
  • Patient destinations are off-site patient tools, such as the portal. Changing an address here updates every link to it. Show In Directory also lists it in the footer and Contact panel.
  • Clinicians holds Clinician roles, the Founder and the Clinician profile links shown on every profile.
  • Site structure holds the Page roles (Home page, Team page and Services page) and the Suggested pages shown when an address has no page. Choosing another page for a role moves the role, and old addresses redirect to the new ones.

The shared treatment design is also stored here but edited inside page sections (see Pages and sections).

Header

Each row in Nav Items has a Placement:

  • In the menu puts a link in the rounded bar. Its Sub Items become a dropdown. Show as a button in the mobile menu moves it below the menu list on phones.
  • As a tab above the menu adds a tab to the row above the bar.
  • At the right end of the tab row adds a small link beside the phone number, such as the patient portal.

Main tab names the first tab in that row, which links to the home page. It appears once any item is a tab.

These links form a section groups the item's page with every page under it by Parent page. The submenu then shows as a bar below the header, unless Hide the bar below the header is ticked; a tab shows it in the rounded bar. The section's pages share the Sidebar CTA Card and Phone bar label in this section set on that row. A tab section can add a Name beside the logo, a Secondary CTA and a CTA.

The Header's own CTA and Secondary CTA are the buttons in the rounded bar on pages no tab section claims. On phones, a bar fixed to the bottom of every page has a Call button for the practice phone, and Phone call bar sets its second button.

Footer

The Footer holds the Tagline, the Column headings, the Location links under the locations, the link Columns, the Social links, the Legal Line and the Legal Links. Locations, phone, email and patient destinations come from Site Settings.

Chapter 14 of 14 · Publishing

Questions and checks

When to ask Andy, common surprises, and a checklist for any change.

Ask Andy

The admin covers content, and content changes happen only in the live admin at https://www.threeriversmentalhealth.com/admin (see The admin at a glance). Send these to Andy instead:

  • Changes to the site's code, and anything else that needs a deploy.
  • Design changes the admin has no control for.
  • A new kind of section. The admin's section types are built in code, so a new one can't be added from the admin.
  • A new field, or a new kind of record.
  • Bringing back something deleted. Versions can't restore a deleted item or an uploaded file.
  • Anything the admin refuses that the message doesn't explain.

Common surprises

  • A private page shows Page not found. That's expected: its public address shows a 404 to everyone, including you while you're signed in. Use View page or Live Preview to see it, or untick Private and save to publish it. See Private, publish and history.
  • A save answers "save again in a minute". A code deploy is running. Keep the tab open, wait a minute and save again, as The admin at a glance explains. Your edits stay in the form.
  • The page looks unchanged after a save. Check that you're on the live site, www.threeriversmentalhealth.com, and not a preview or a local copy. The dashboard's Open the site button goes there. Then refresh the page. If it still looks old, tell Andy which page, what you changed and when you saved.
  • A section on a service page shows nothing. A Care team section stays hidden until a clinician's Services provided include its service, and a Care pathways section stays hidden until the service has Care pathways rows. A private service also drops out of other pages' cards and pathways. See Services.
  • A save or delete is refused because something uses the record. Messages such as "Still chosen as a service" and "is still used" name the places that choose it. Change those first, then try again (see Where content lives).
  • A save stops with "Not saved. The Private checkbox also saves Site Settings". Fix the Site Settings fields the message names, then save the record again.
  • Change slug… won't run. The admin asks you to save or discard your other changes first, because the slug change saves on its own. See Addresses and moving pages.

Asking a good question

Tell Andy the page or record title, its address, what you meant to do and what happened. Copy any message exactly, say when you saved, and add a screenshot of the control.

Check your work

Run through this for any change.
